chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim narrated from al-Amiri, from Safwan, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Know that prayer is disliked (makruh) in three places on the Baida' road, which are Dhat al-Jaysh, Dhat al-Salasil, and Padjanan."
And he said, "There is no harm in praying between the Zawahir (raised edges/ridges), which are the Jawadd (highways/main roads) of the paths, but it is disliked to pray inside the Jawadd."
And it is recommended to complete the prayers in the two Harams (Mecca and Medina), for indeed in them is much virtue. Narrated.

key_terms.الطَّرِيقِ الْبَيْدَاءِ: The Baida' Road - a specific historical road near Mecca
key_terms.الظَّوَاهِرِ: The Zawahir - the raised edges or ridges of the road
key_terms.الْجَوَادُّ: The Jawadd - the main, high, or wide part of the road
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Harams - referring to Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and Masjid al-Nabi in Medina
key_terms.تُكْرَهُ: Disliked (makruh) - a legal ruling indicating preference for avoidance but not prohibition
key_terms.ذَاتُ الْجَيْشِ: Dhat al-Jaysh - one of the three specific locations mentioned

ai.seo_question: Where is it disliked to pray on the road according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the juristic nuances of praying on roads, distinguishing between the disliked areas of the Baida' road (specifically Dhat al-Jaysh, Dhat al-Sasalil, and Dajan) and the permissible raised edges (Zawahir). It highlights the scholarly preference for completing prayers within the two holy sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina) to maximize spiritual reward, reflecting the broader Shia emphasis on the sanctity of specific geographic spaces in ritual practice.
